conventions.convention: Basic-Cohen continuity: "ordinal-definable from A and a fixed finite tuple u" means unique coded definability from the predicate A, the tuple u and finitely many ordinal parameters; the varied tuple must be disjoint from rng(u), and its basic clopen neighbourhoods are pairwise disjoint and avoid rng(u).
The supported-ideal lemma claims maximality only among proper ideals in the same A,f-supported definability class, never maximality among all ideals of B; the item states this restriction explicitly.

Feferman-Levy system: ground V |= ZFC+GCH, kappa_n = aleph_n^V, P the finite-support product of Col(omega,kappa_n); the group is the layer-preserving finite permutations of omega x omega, H_m is pointwise identity on layers n<m, and "m-bounded layer support" means fixed by H_m.
Support extraction is per name: every hereditarily symmetric name is fixed by one H_m, and only one such m is chosen at a time (no simultaneous support selection for a family).

B_m is the complete subalgebra of H_m-fixed Boolean values and is identified with the complete subalgebra generated by conditions restricted to layers n<m (conditions identified with their canonical nonzero regular-open values).

The real layers are R_m = {x-dot_G : x-dot in S_m} with S_m the ground set of Boolean names of the form {<k-check,b_k> : k<omega}, b_k in B_m; both the layers and the sequence <R_m> are asserted to be sets of N, while no simultaneous enumeration of the layers is claimed.

Feferman's tail-flip system uses all bit flips 2^(omega x omega), not only finite ones, with H_m trivial on the first m predicates; M* = union_m M_m with permitted parameters ordinals plus (S_0,...,S_{m-1}); the sequence <S_n> itself is not a permitted parameter; "complement modulo finite" means symmetric difference with a finite set.

The tail flip is taken at coordinate n+1 above k_0 = 1 + max{k : (n+1,k) in dom(Q)}, with k_0 = 0 when that domain is empty, so the flip fixes Q and all earlier-coordinate parameters and sends S_{n+1} to its complement modulo the finite initial segment {k : k<k_0}.

Blass model: delta(x) = {y : x triangle y finite}; f(n) = {delta(a_n), delta(omega \ a_n)}; S = union_n(delta(a_n) union delta(omega \ a_n)) union {f} (so S consists of reals plus the single parameter f); N consists of the x in M[G] whose transitive closure is uniquely definable from f, finitely many members of S\{f} and finitely many ordinals; S is definable from f and acts as a reservoir of finitely many parameters, not as one pointwise parameter.

Measurability in the small-forcing theorem is the local notion: kappa uncountable and carrying a nonprincipal ultrafilter closed under intersections of length below kappa; the same item supplies the normal-ultrapower embedding direction and the seed-measure direction.

Finitistic trees have finite levels, a root, finite linearly ordered predecessor sets and no terminal nodes; A is (h,k)-dense iff some x in T(h) is such that A dominates every node of T(h+k) above x, k-dense means (0,k)-dense; an (h,k)-matrix is a product of coordinatewise (h,k)-dense sets and need not lie in the level product; the dimension d is positive.

L_d consists of the length-2d words containing for each coordinate i exactly one legal ordered pair (exists A_i before forall x_i, or forall a_i before exists x_i); Rule 3 applies only to adjacent blocks and only when both displayed words lie in L_d; derivability is the reflexive-transitive closure of Rules 1-3 and is purely syntactic.

A finite partial prime-ideal diagram is a Boolean homomorphism on a whole finite Boolean subalgebra (the cells are its nonzero atoms), not an arbitrary truth assignment consistent with finitely many displayed equations; the empty list generates {0,1}.

The countable compactness-tree conclusion is a ZF theorem for a Boolean algebra supplied with a specified surjection b: omega onto B, obtained by a definable bit-preference branch (no Konig's lemma, no choice); the AC hypothesis is reserved for the finite-level partition theorem, where it is declared.

Solovay ground is V = L^U for an ambient ZFC model U with inaccessible kappa (kappa stays inaccessible in V); P = Lv(kappa) consists of finite p with dom(p) subset of kappa x omega and p(alpha,n)<alpha; P_xi = {p : dom(p) subset xi x omega}, G_xi = G cap P_xi; Choice is a ground/ambient hypothesis only.

S = union_{alpha in Ord} {}^omega alpha (so every real is an S-parameter after identifying naturals with finite ordinals); M = HOD(S) = {x : tc({x}) subset of OD(S)} with one S-parameter plus finitely many ordinals, finite/countable tuples interleaved by a fixed pairing; no equality with L(R) or HOD(R) is asserted.

L(R) is defined by L_0(R) = tc({R}), L_{alpha+1}(R) = Def(L_alpha(R), in, R cap L_alpha(R)) with unions at limits; only the inclusion L(R) subset of HOD(S) is asserted, the reverse inclusion and any identification with HOD(R) are not.

Absoluteness discipline: coded nullness, meagreness, openness and closedness are absolute in the directions used; coded nonemptiness and perfectness transfer only between models with the same reals or from an explicit pruned splitting-tree certificate (a closed code may gain branches in an outer model with new reals).

The final Solovay statement is the one-way implication Con(ZFC + an inaccessible) => Con(ZF+DC+universal LM+BP+PSP+not-AC); no converse and no internal inaccessible is asserted, and the designated kappa becomes omega_1 in both inner models.

load_bearing.statement: Let M be a transitive model of ZFC, G M-generic for Add(omega,omega)^M, N = HS^G the basic Cohen model. Then every proper set filter in N extends in N to an ultrafilter; consequently every nontrivial Boolean algebra in N has a prime ideal (proved through the stated finite-support filter-extension property).
N = HS^G is a transitive model of ZF + BPI + not-AC; its symmetric set A of coordinate Cohen reals is infinite and Dedekind-finite, and in particular is not well-orderable in N.

Every hereditarily symmetric name in the Feferman-Levy system is fixed by H_m for some m<omega. In particular, every real in the symmetric model N has a name whose Boolean values are all fixed by one such H_m.

For B = RO(P) and B_m the complete subalgebra of H_m-fixed values, u = join{p restricted to m : p in P and p <=_B u}, and B_m is exactly the complete subalgebra generated by conditions using only layers n<m.
In the Feferman-Levy model N, R^N = union_{m<omega} R_m, and every R_m is countable; thus the set of all reals is a countable union of countable sets.

Definition of the all-bit-flip symmetric system over Add(omega,omega) with H_m trivial on the first m predicates, of M_m (sets hereditarily definable from ordinals and (S_0,...,S_{m-1})) and M* = union_m M_m, together with the asserted identification of M* with the hereditarily symmetric interpretation HS_F^G.

For a finite condition Q and a definition using only S_0,...,S_n and ordinal parameters there is k_0 with the automorphism fixing every coordinate other than n+1 and flipping S_{n+1}(k) for all k >= k_0 fixing Q and all the definition's parameters while sending S_{n+1} to its complement modulo the finite initial segment k_0.
In M*(S_0,S_1,...), every prime ideal of the Boolean algebra P(omega) is principal.

Definition of the finite-modification classes delta(x), the function f(n) = {delta(a_n), delta(omega\a_n)}, the parameter reservoir S = union_n(delta(a_n) union delta(omega\a_n)) union {f}, and the parameter-HOD class N of sets whose transitive closure is uniquely definable from f, finitely many members of S\{f} and finitely many ordinals.

Assume ZFC. Let P be a forcing notion in V, G V-generic, and kappa an uncountable cardinal with |P|^V < kappa. If V[G] regards kappa as measurable (locally: uncountable and carrying a nonprincipal ultrafilter closed under intersections of length below kappa), then V already regards kappa as measurable.
In Blass's parameter-HOD model N, every ultrafilter on every set is principal.

In ZF, let d>0, T_1,...,T_d finitistic trees and Q a subset of the full product. At least one of the following holds: (1) for every k<omega, Q contains a k-matrix; (2) for some h<omega and every k<omega, the complement of Q in the full product contains an (h,k)-matrix.

Let A subset of C be finite Boolean subalgebras of a Boolean algebra B. Every homomorphism e: A -> 2 extends to a homomorphism e': C -> 2; consequently every finite partial prime-ideal diagram extends to one deciding any prescribed finite subset of B.
Over ZF, the Boolean prime ideal principle is equivalent to the set ultrafilter lemma: every proper filter of subsets of a set extends to an ultrafilter on that set.

Definition of the Solovay ground V = L^U with inaccessible kappa, of P = Lv(kappa) = Coll(omega,<kappa), its initial suborders P_xi, the generic restrictions G_xi and the quotient P/G_xi, with Choice confined to the ground.
In V[G], kappa = omega_1; every real and every function f: omega -> Ord belongs to some V[G_xi], xi<kappa; and R^{V[G_xi]} is countable in V[G].

M = HOD(S) is a transitive ZF inner model with the same ordinals and reals as V[G]. Every A subset of R in M is definable in V[G] from a real and finitely many ordinals, equivalently from one countable ordinal sequence.

Shared well-founded Borel codes evaluate identically on shared reals; every Borel code uniformly yields a coded open set modulo a coded meagre set; coded nullness, meagreness, openness and closedness are absolute in the directions used; coded nonemptiness and perfectness transfer only between models with the same reals or from an explicit pruned splitting-tree certificate.

Let N be ambient-countable, Q in N a small collapse, p in Q, and tau-dot in N a Q-name with p forcing tau-dot in R\N. In V[G] there is a perfect binary tree of Q-generics containing p, mutually generic in every pair of distinct branches, whose tau-dot-interpretations are pairwise distinct and vary continuously.

concerns.concern: F2 orders the definition codes "first by formula code, then by rank, and then lexicographically by the finite ordinal tuple" and cites lem-canonical-well-order-of-finite-definition-codes, whose statement orders codes by formula code and then lexicographically by the tuple of the arity fixed by that code, with no rank coordinate. The order actually used is still a well-order (for each formula code the pairs (rank, tuple) are well-ordered by rank and then lex), and unique least codes still exist, but the minimization argument is not the one displayed in the cited lemma and must be re-run for the stated order.

This item's deps and body use only thm-halpern-lauchli-dense-matrix-dichotomy and thm-basic-cohen-model-satisfies-bpi-and-fails-choice, but the unified dependency ledger still carries open rows from it to lem-basic-cohen-model-schema-of-continuity, cor-basic-cohen-model-finite-set-continuity and lem-ordinal-definable-maximal-proper-ideal-in-the-basic-cohen-model (declared in the batch-8 pages manifest). Steps 1.1-2.1 explicitly say the parameter-definable-maximal-ideal route is not used, so those rows need to be resolved to removed (or the dependencies reinstated) before the Step-8 ledger reconciliation.

Step 1.1 verifies ZF for the parameter-HOD class N in five sentences, citing thm-hod-is-an-inner-model-containing-l for the "same checks ... relativized below to f and finitely many members of S". The delicate clause is Replacement: for f, x in N the image set must be shown to be definable from f and the hereditary codes of x (not from per-value codes), with TC of the image inside OD(S). The ordinary HOD argument does close this, using that S is definable from f, but the step as written asserts the closure rather than displaying it.

Steps 9.1-13.1 rest on the asserted identity N = W (W the least class of singletons closed under ordinal-indexed unions) and on the rank bookkeeping that keeps the partition pieces Y_alpha at strictly lower W-rank. Step 12.1 compresses the N subset of W direction into "the code space is a subset of a finite product and a well-ordered union of theta^{<omega}, omega and S^{<omega}"; that evaluation-map argument and the rank decrease in step 13.1 are where the induction could fail and are not fully written out.

Steps 3.1-8.1 compress Hamkins' gap-forcing restriction argument (ground part M = union_alpha j(V_alpha), j(G) = G, the fresh-sequence obstruction, the common-cover claim for delta-sized sets of ordinals, the identification V cap M[G] = M, and amenability of j restricted to V). I checked the statement, the local measurability definition, the ultrapower direction of step 1.2 and the final Scott-style contradiction (the least measurable cardinal is parameter-free definable, so elementarity with Q_0 = M forces j(lambda) = lambda), but I did not independently reproduce steps 4.2, 5.1, 6.1, 7.1 or 7.2.

Step 2.1 says "The construction has a real code; since M has all reals, that code lies in M, and F6 says internally that P is nonempty perfect." The tree produced in lem-solovay-perfect-tree-of-mutually-generic-name-interpretations is an ambient omega-sequence of conditions in the bounded stage N (hence in M by the closure lemma), and P is then definable in M from that tree and the forcing relation; the phrase "has a real code" is doing the work of that coding argument, which is not displayed, and lem-solovay-borel-code-and-regularity-absoluteness transfers nonemptiness/perfectness only from an explicit pruned splitting-tree certificate.

F1 is "def-feferman-tail-flip-definability-model identifies the ranked finite-predicate union M* with HS_F^G for that exact symmetric system". That identification is a substantive two-sided equivalence (the reverse direction is Feferman's tail homogeneity plus V = L), but it is asserted inside a definition item whose provenance is not-applicable, with only a one-sentence sketch; the ZF theorem then consumes it as given. A judge should treat the equivalence itself, not only the transfer through the published symmetric-model theorem, as the load-bearing claim.

Steps 1.3, 1.4 and 5.1 invoke "the reduction in Appendix C of Ransom's source to the cited Todorcevic-Farah compatible-type lemma" and the spreading/gathering maps of Ransom Section 5. I confirmed bibliographically that arXiv:2511.21684 exists (Nov 2025) and that its ToC contains the filter extension property, Theorem 4.9, Appendix C (proof of Lemma 4.6) and the Sigma/Gamma maps of Section 5, but I could not read the source argument itself, so the finite compatible-type reduction and the reindexing collapse are taken on the strength of the citation.

seams_checked.note: The edge is declared at page level (requires: ["large-cardinals-measures-and-elementary-embeddings", "symmetric-collapse-and-ultrafilter-free-models"] in the batch-9 pages manifest, marked verified in research/phase-2-next-18-cross-batch-dependencies.json). No item of the Gitik page cites any item of my page: I checked all 20 batch-9 items and their wikilinks, and the symmetric-model work there goes through the published general theorem thm-hereditarily-symmetric-interpretations-form-a-zf-model (plus def-symmetric-forcing-system-and-hereditarily-symmetric-names, def-forcing-name-automorphism-action and lem-symmetry-lemma-for-forcing-automorphisms), not through the Feferman-Levy, Feferman or Blass items. I opened thm-gitik-symmetric-submodel-satisfies-zf: its F5 ("Each set-forcing symmetric interpretation is a transitive ZF model, and its choice-free proof supplies the transitive almost-universal-class criterion used below") restates the cited statement ("For a transitive ZF ground model M, symmetric system and M-generic G_0, N = HS^G_0 is a transitive ZF model with M subset of N subset of M[G_0]. No Choice hypothesis is required") with the same hypotheses, direction and conclusion, and its closing caution ("No choice function used in the ground or intermediate construction is thereby made an element of N_G, and Choice is not part of the conclusion") matches my page's convention that Choice occurs only in the ambient construction. So the citing text is faithful; there is simply no restatement of my page's content for the seam to distort, and the page-level prerequisite is discharged by the published general theorem.
